findings.title: Address-evidence test expects a nonmatch for a checksum-invalid address; CI fails on main
findings.releaseBlockingReason: pnpm test, pnpm verify and the GitHub CI gate fail on main
findings.reproduction: Run pnpm test at 7b059c7, or open GitHub Actions run 36331656864.
findings.expected: The suite passes; a checksum-invalid address either errors clearly before the date search or is a nonmatch, and the test asserts the chosen contract.
findings.observed: The AUD-001-FUN001 fix canonicalises evidence through Address(network).decode, which throws 'Invalid checksum in bc1qcr8te4kr609gcawutmrza0j4xv80jy8z306fyq' for the test's corrupted 'different address'. 1 failed / 319 passed locally and in CI runs 36328965890 and 36331656864.
findings.impact: Every mandatory gate is red, so new regressions cannot be distinguished from this known failure. Production behaviour (fail fast on malformed evidence) is defensible; the defect is the stale assertion and the unwrapped error.
findings.recommendedFix: Expect an error for the corrupted address; use a genuinely different valid address (for example the index-1 BIP84 address) for the nonmatch case; wrap decode failures in a MnemoCode message (see AUD-002-API002). Do not relax validation.
findings.requiredVerification: pnpm test and CI green; the uppercase case in known-audit-defects.test.ts still passes; a new test covers corrupted-checksum evidence.

findings.title: Share, WIF and passphrase files bypass the 1 MiB text-input budget
findings.reproduction: Create a 3 MiB --share-file or --wif-file and run sskr-combine or recover-date with public data.
findings.expected: Local file inputs share the documented 1 MiB budget and fail before the whole file is read.
findings.observed: Both files are read completely (maxrss 183 MB and 116 MB) and rejected only by the downstream parser. No suite test mentions any input limit.
findings.impact: Bounded: user-chosen file, no secret exposure, process exits. Inconsistent with the AUD-001-SEC003 intent rather than a demonstrated exhaustion.
findings.recommendedFix: Route the three reads through readBoundedTextFile; add tests for the text, stdin, PNG-byte, PNG-dimension and share-file limits.
findings.requiredVerification: Over-limit share, WIF and passphrase files fail with the safety-limit message before parsing; limit tests pass.

findings.title: CLI integer options accept JavaScript numeric syntax inconsistently with the index parser
findings.expected: Decimal integers only, matching parseInput for indexes and integer() in sskr-command.ts.
findings.observed: Number(raw) accepts hexadecimal, exponent and padded forms: 0x10 selects word 16, 1e3 selects word 1000, 0x2 is accepted.
findings.impact: A mistyped value can silently select a different valid index; no secret exposure.
findings.recommendedFix: One shared strict integer parser with bounds for all numeric options.
findings.requiredVerification: The three forms are rejected naming the option; decimal values still work.

findings.title: Malformed evidence and destination inputs surface raw dependency or OS errors
findings.reproduction: recover-date with a testnet address on mainnet; a corrupted address; --pdf DIR/all.pdf where DIR is a not-yet-existing --cards-dir; a missing --mnemonic-file.
findings.expected: Project messages naming the option and problem without echoing the value.
findings.observed: 'Invalid checksum in bc1q...' echoes the supplied address; 'Unknown letter "0". Allowed: ...' for a testnet address on mainnet; 'invalid length' for an oversized WIF; 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath ...' for the nested destination.
findings.impact: Usability and consistency; addresses are public identifiers, so no secret disclosure, but the project's redaction policy elsewhere avoids echoing input.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate evidence at option parsing and map decode failures to project messages; let effectiveOutputPath tolerate a not-yet-existing parent chain; report missing input files by option name.
findings.requiredVerification: Each reproduction prints a project message; uppercase and typo probes keep their results.

findings.title: QR PNG input reads IHDR dimensions without checking the PNG signature
findings.reproduction: mnemocode decode --qr-file notpng.png where the file contains 43 bytes of text.
findings.expected: 'The QR input is not a PNG file.'
findings.observed: Bytes 16-24 are read as width and height, so the message is the 4096 px / 16-megapixel limit error; a zero-width PNG reports the same message.
findings.impact: Misleading diagnostics only; pngjs still rejects the file and the 16 MiB byte limit applies first.
findings.recommendedFix: Verify the 8-byte signature and the IHDR chunk type before reading dimensions; keep the size and pixel limits.
findings.requiredVerification: Non-PNG, truncated and zero-dimension inputs each produce their own message; valid QR PNGs still decode.

findings.title: Audit records and README still present all six AUD-001 findings as open
findings.reproduction: Compare the AUD-001 remediation table (all open, 'six it.fails tests') with test/known-audit-defects.test.ts and test/self-test-integrity.test.ts (ordinary tests) and with this audit's disposition table.
findings.expected: A remediation follow-up recording four production findings as verified and AUD-001-SEC001/AUD-001-FUN001 as fixed pending completion of their original verification requirements, with fix and verification commits where established, a dated evidence note, and an index/README without the obsolete six-open-expected-failures claim.
findings.observed: The records still describe the pre-fix snapshot as current; the README's audit paragraph repeats it. This audit confirms fixes for all six but fully verifies only four.
findings.impact: Readers cannot distinguish fixed code from fully verified remediation, and the newly reproduced blocker AUD-002-BLD001 is absent from the older records.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the follow-up and evidence note to AUD-001 (Markdown and JSON together, preserving original observations), update docs/audits/README.md and README.md:619, record four verified findings, two fixed-but-not-verified findings, and AUD-002-BLD001 as the current newly reproduced blocker. Remediated code enters the rewritten history at 7b08fc2, af8655c and e591a2d; verification snapshot 7b059c7.
findings.requiredVerification: JSON validates without duplicate keys; Markdown and JSON statuses agree; the evidence note names the commands re-run.

findings.title: Maintained documentation drifted from the code and toolchain
findings.reproduction: Read the cited lines against src/cli/qr-input.ts:5-7, package.json and the README install section.
findings.expected: Limits, pinned versions and package-manager commands described consistently.
findings.observed: REVIEW says PNG input has no size or pixel limit although 16 MiB, 4096 px and 16 Mpx limits exist; the CHANGELOG toolchain entry omits Prettier 3.9.9 and the pnpm 10.19.0 pin; ARCHITECTURE and one README example use npm run while the install section and CI use pnpm.
findings.impact: Minor reader confusion; no behavioural effect.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the three statements; add Prettier and pnpm to the CHANGELOG entry.

findings.title: AUD-001 evidence integrity manifest no longer matches 47 reformatted files
findings.expected: The bundle's manifest verifies, or the evidence README states which entries were altered and why.
findings.observed: 47 of 109 entries fail; all are JSON or JavaScript now in Prettier's style (Prettier ran before docs/audits/ was added to .prettierignore). All 25 command-log hashes still match. The original bytes are not in Git.
findings.impact: The retained-evidence integrity claim is false for those entries although their content is semantically unchanged.
findings.recommendedFix: Record the reformatting in the evidence README with date and affected entries, regenerate SHA256SUMS from current bytes with that note, keep docs/audits/ formatter-ignored.
findings.requiredVerification: sha256sum -c passes and the README explains the regeneration.

observations.title: Readability is good; geometry, colour and content-validation helpers are duplicated
observations.reproduction: Source inspection and counts; not a reproduced defect.
observations.expected: Shared page geometry, colour-space and content-validation helpers; QR PNG writer under export/.
observations.observed: MM defined three times; page-dimension table three times as nested ternaries; hsv() twice and rgb() inlined; validateContent three times with differing messages; two fit() helpers; color-export.ts imports cli/qr-export.ts. TypeScript 7.0.2 compiles with 0 diagnostics; 77 non-null assertions, 11 nested ternaries, 0 any, 0 suppressions, 0 TODO; 130 comment lines in 7 819 explain invariants and units. Longest functions: printUsage 316 (help text), main 144, runPreview 100.
observations.impact: Divergence risk between renderers; no functional defect.
observations.recommendedFix: Add export/page-geometry.ts, export/color-space.ts and export/card-content.ts; move qr-export.ts under export/; keep family renderers and printUsage otherwise intact.
observations.requiredVerification: pnpm check, pnpm format:check and the render matrix unchanged; business goldens pixel-identical.

observations.title: Canonical SSKR WASM rebuild is byte-identical; host builds differ; platform matrix remains
observations.reproduction: Build vendor/sskr/rust (source, lockfile and manifest hashes identical to multi-chain-wallet-tools packages/recovery-sskr-wasm) inside the sibling repository's pinned Dockerfile.reproducible with networking disabled, using its build-recovery-sskr-wasm.mjs; compare with the committed files. Repeat on the host.
observations.expected: Byte-identical generated files from the documented canonical environment.
observations.observed: Container (Node 26.10.0, Rust 1.98.1, clang 18.1.3, wasm-bindgen 0.2.128): all four files identical. Host (clang 21.1.8): code section 213 360 versus 219 227 bytes, functionally equivalent on the official vector and a zero-seed deterministic split.
observations.impact: Closes the canonical-rebuild part of AUD-001-BLD002 for the SSKR module; crate provenance beyond Cargo.lock checksums and Windows/macOS/other Node versions remain unverified.
observations.recommendedFix: Document the container rebuild as the only supported regeneration path; add a second-OS CI job running pnpm verify.
observations.requiredVerification: Retained container log with toolchain identity and identical hashes; second-OS CI green.

observations.title: Input budgets and secret lifecycle verified within stated limits
observations.reproduction: Over-limit and crafted inputs through the CLI; source trace of finally-block cleanup and staged publication.
observations.expected: Limits enforced before allocation; owned buffers cleared; exports staged privately and published atomically; hidden input refuses without a controlling terminal.
observations.observed: All verified for text, stdin and PNG inputs and for entropy, random seed, decoded WIF, restored SSKR secret and BIP32 nodes; exports 0600/0700.
observations.impact: Residual: JavaScript strings holding mnemonics, shares and WIF text cannot be erased; systemd-ask-password is Linux-specific; no allocation-failure or renderer-timeout injection.
observations.recommendedFix: See AUD-002-SEC001 for the file-input gap; document the string-erasure limit (already present in REVIEW.md).

remediation.note: The follow-up passes local gates, a fresh registry audit and GitHub Actions run 36338523182.
Commit b71aff4 adds BIP86, different-valid-address, checksum, mixed-case and wrong-network regression coverage and passes GitHub CI.
Unchanged since AUD-001; the three corrected assertions still pass.

limitations: Full-scope audit with every procedure area assigned an outcome; Linux x86_64 and Node 26.10.0 only.
Only public or synthetic secrets were used; no wallet material, network transaction, push, release or external message.
The Rust bridge source was read and rebuilt, not cryptographically reviewed; crate provenance rests on Cargo.lock checksums.
Visual checks were construction, dimension and QR-decode checks on rasterised pages; no physical print or camera test.
Fault injection (RNG failure, interrupted writes, renderer timeout, full disk) was not executed.

One harness mistake (PNG files rasterised as PDFs) and its correction are retained; one sub-check of the first SSKR probe mis-mapped members and was superseded by fragment-qr-check.json. Neither is a product defect.
The Prettier documentation check failed on NOTICE for lack of a parser; this is a harness limitation, the project's own format:check passed.

Five retained .log files lack command companions: three are batch-progress summaries, environment.log is a standalone environment capture, and typecheck-sskr-only-without-types-node.log is an intermediate-tree result that is not used as finding evidence.
The clean-at-start assertion in snapshot.json lacks a timestamped raw git status log; environment.log was captured later and records one uncommitted entry after evidence collection had begun.
Reasoning effort is not retained by the client and is recorded as null; the session was forked once and continued on the same snapshot.
Machine-local paths in command companions describe where evidence was produced; temporary workspaces were deleted.

gaps: No suite test covers the 1 MiB, 16 MiB, 4096 px or 16 Mpx limits; share/WIF/passphrase files have no limit.
Bitcoin evidence tests use BIP84 mainnet index 0 only; BIP44/49/86, testnet, non-zero locations, WIF and xpub paths are audit probes only.
Checksum-valid Seedshift vectors for 15-24 words lack fingerprints; no second independent implementation beyond the in-test oracle.
Rasterised QR readability checked for representative templates only; no physical print or camera test.
